angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,625,155 km at 80.04 pc = 0.27 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 12.4934 +/- 0.0170 mas (same row, RUWE 0.98): 80.04 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 2.336 +/- 0.052 solar radii from Nielsen et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 1397 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...623A.100N/abstract): 1,625,155 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.324 +/- 0.042 solar masses from Nielsen et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 1397 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...623A.100N/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5521 +/- 60 K from Nielsen et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 1397 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...623A.100N/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Nielsen et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 1397 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...623A.100N/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-1397.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 3.823, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
